small_guidance:
- The fused pool+LSE+ReLU kernel is already cheap; the dominant cost is the Conv3d. Tuning the fused kernel further (TILE_W sweeps 32/64/128, num_warps 4/8) will not move fast_p much. If staying small, drop the `x.contiguous()` after conv (do the channels_last→contiguous copy inside the fused kernel via strided loads) to remove one full tensor copy.
- Add `triton.autotune` over (TILE_W ∈ {32,64,128}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}) keyed on (N,Do,Ho,Wo) for the fused kernel.
- Verify channels_last_3d actually triggers cuDNN's NHWC kernels here; if not, fall back to NCDHW — the explicit `.to(channels_last_3d)` round-trip on input may add overhead without a kernel switch.
large_guidance:
- Conv3d dominates runtime (~20ms vs 6.7ms baseline → conv alone is ≥6ms). Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), gather the 3×3×3×IC window with computed offsets, accumulate into a BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N tile, and fuse the 2×2×2 maxpool + LSE-over-C + ReLU directly into the epilogue so the OC-dim tile is reduced in-register without writing the conv output.
- Better: tile the kernel over output positions at pool-output granularity (each program owns one 2×2×2 pool window across all OC), compute all 8 conv outputs for the full OC vector, take max over the 8, then do online LSE reduction across OC, then ReLU — single kernel, conv output never materialized, avoids the 4×64×32×128×128 intermediate (128MB).
- Pre-pack weights to (OC, IC*kd*kh*kw) at init for contiguous K-dim loads; use channels-last input layout so IC is the contiguous GEMM-K axis. Autotune BLOCK_OC/BLOCK_SPATIAL/BLOCK_K around (32–64, 16–32, 32–64).
